steps.text: Combine cream and buttermilk in a glass jar. Cover tightly with cheesecloth (or any breathable material) and let sit at room temperature (70 to 75 degrees F (21 to 24 degrees C)) until thickened, about 24 hours.
Stir mixture, then screw on the lid.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Crème Fraîche
raw_recipe.description: Crème fraîche is easy to make at home with heavy cream and buttermilk. It has a fabulous taste and texture far superior to store-bought sour cream.
raw_recipe.name: Chef John's Crème Fraîche

review.reviewBody: This is a marvelous recipe! I could put it on almost any food in my fridge! I found the correct cream at Trader Joe's, an organic one, and my buttermilk was by Knudsen. I was just going to make a half a batch but went for the whole thing. Am I ever glad! This is better than sour cream! Creme Fraiche doesn't have the same holding power of sour cream as far as consistency goes, and it's not quite as sour. But delicious it is! I highly recommend that you try this! Thank you, Chef John!

Ultra-pasteurized heavy whipping cream works just fine. I use it exclusively and it has never failed to make great Creme Fraiche. Don't waste your time looking for pasteurized. I use Ball canning jars to make this great sour cream in and will never buy another plastic tub of it.

I used 1 1/2 cup Whipping Cream (jar was too small for all of the whipping cream) and 2 tablespoons Seco Cultured Buttermilk powder. I used the Seco powder as it is Cultured and I did not want to have wasted buttermilk in my fridge. In my local store the heavy cream was ultra pasteurized but the whipping cream was regular pasteurized so I used the regular cream. I started the culture around 5 pm and tasted it the next morning around 7 am. It tasted like sweet whipping cream so I left it alone. When I tasted it at 2 pm - ZING big difference and it tasted as described but it was still thin. I put the lid on the jar and put it in the fridge and let it thicken. Bottom line - use the powder and you won't have to deal with a quart of liquid leftover buttermilk. Try this and see. Your results may vary..........

Ultra pasterized heavy whipping cream worked just fine with the requisite cultured buttermilk. Washed and sterilized a quart mason jar, letting it "air dry" to avoid contaminating. Shake the cream and pour in (1 pint = 2 cups) and shake the container of buttermilk and add the 3T. Covered with a clean new tea bag and elastic band. It's summer so plenty warm but I placed it into the water used to sterilize the jar (it was 110 degrees), it cooled quickly and then put it in my microwave overnight. Checked it in the morning - it was already thick and gorgeous. Gave it a stir and a taste after 14 hours and it's perfection already. Going to pop into the fridge tonight following the 24 hour advise. Going to buy more cream to make another batch to use up the remaining buttermilk. So easy and is LITERALLY foolproof!

I've been making creme fraiche using this method for almost 20 years. Easy peasy and SO tasty. It's also good made with Brown Cow yogurt instead of buttermilk (the live cultures are important).

This does work with ultra pasteurized cream, I've done it more than once when ultra pasteurized was all I could find. You may need more buttermilk/yogurt or a little more time for it to culture.

This is terrific! I used ultra-pasteurized cream as that is all I could find, and it worked just fine. This was pretty cool to make, and who knew it was so easy?! I used it to make Creme Caramel and BLT Pasta, both also Chef John's recipes, and both are truly amazing. Thank you, Chef John- you continue to make me look like a culinary genius :)

This is a good recipe although I make mine with equal parts sour cream and heavy (whipping) cream. Mix it well and place in an air tight container and leave on your counter top for 24 hrs then refrigerate. Amazing flavor and texture!!

I loved this! I used 1 tablespoon buttermilk and 1 cup ultra-pasteurized whipping cream. I shook them together in a mason jar, then left out on the counter for 30 hours (I just screwed on the lid and didn't use cheesecloth). It cultured perfectly into a thick, smooth cream like soft sour cream. After chilling the jar overnight in the refrigerator it had the exact consistency of sour cream and was so delicious!

I've made creme fraiche for years and I always keep a pint in the refrigerator for cooking and thickening soups or other creamy sauces. A couple of tips I've learned over the years: start with a clean pint wide mouth jar. Fill with water and microwave until boiling. Allow to sit for a minute, pour out water (WILL BE HOT- CAREFUL!) add buttermilk, then heavy cream. Sterilizing the container prevents harmful molds from forming. If you EVER find pink mold on your creme fraiche, discard & start over. I've only had this happen once and it was when I did not sterilize the jar before making. Second tip- when you have consumed almost all of your creme fraiche, You do not need to buy buttermilk again to make more. As long as you have a tablespoon or two left in the jar, simply add several oz. Of heavy cream, stir well scraping the sides of the jar. When you feel you have mixed the remaining residue into your new heavy cream, top off the jar, stir well, cover with a breathable cloth, and allow to sit overnight or longer. Check the next day, stir well, and if it has thickened, refrigerate until ready for use. Following this regimen will allow you to keep an almost indefinite supply of creme fraiche ready for use. Beneficial bacteria that creates the creme fraiche retards spoilage as long as you keep the finished product refrigerated. Once again, beware of the pink mold! It IS HARMFUL!

Great flavor and simple to make. I put the sterilized jar in a card board box with an LED light bulb for 24 hours and the temperature was between 73 - 75 degrees. I also used Cacique Mexican brand Cream. It was the only Pasteurized cream I could find at my local store. Good stuff and just in time for Super Bowl street taco's!!

I used ultra pasteurized heavy whipping cream because that’s what I could easily find, and the store branded buttermilk. Put the jar in the oven with the light on for 24 hours. I guess I didn’t pay close attention because I put a mason jar lid on it rather than a coffee filter. Then refrigerated it for 24 hours. Couldn’t have come out more perfect! And so easy! BTW I tried it in my Instant Pot on the yogurt setting for 8 hours too. My yogurt comes out perfect, but for some reason the creme fraiche did not. It never set up. If I want pourable creme fraiche then the IP method is certainly faster and it still tasted great.

EZ! 1. Pour, pour, stir. 2. Cover & Wait 24 hrs 3. Stir 4. Seal w/lid 5. Fridge 24 hrs 💝Finiti! ✅Great for cheesecakes and flammekuchen 💝. I have been using this recipe for 15 years it’s perfect. Never fails me.
Love it so so much thank you
Great taste, smooth and creamy. Easy to make.
I struggle to not eat this out of the jar. Sooo good, and you can eat on nearly anything. Sweet or savory. Better than sour cream! Thanks Chef!
Made this and it’s sooo good! It’s a keeper!

Made this as directed. I tested it with a carbonara. OMG! IT IS JUST PERFECT! I am saying good bye to the store bought from now on. It is not only less expensive but the flavor is just downright better. I used Bulgarian style cultured buttermilk and the result is FANTASTIC. I thought I had bought the crème fraîche D' Isigny I used to buy in France. I can totally bet a stroganoff will also be fantastic. Will report on it!

It did not turn out for me. I think because my house wasreally cold. I forgot to turn the heat on before I went to work. My question now is can I take it out of the refrigerator step and let it warm up for a second time ? Or will it spoil?
